questions.question: Who designed the flag that became the basis of India's National Flag?
questions.rationale: Pingali Venkayya's design, refined with Gandhi's input (the charkha later replaced by the Ashoka Chakra), was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 22 July 1947.

questions.question: How many spokes does the Ashoka Chakra on the National Flag have?
questions.rationale: The navy-blue wheel has 24 spokes — one for each hour of the day — taken from the Lion Capital of Sarnath. The clock-face 12 is the classic trap option.

questions.question: The National Anthem of India, 'Jana Gana Mana', was first sung on:
questions.rationale: Tagore's Bengali original was sung at the Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress on 27 December 1911; it was adopted as the National Anthem on 24 January 1950.

questions.question: The words 'Satyameva Jayate' on the State Emblem are taken from which Upanishad?
questions.rationale: 'Truth alone triumphs' appears in the Mundaka Upanishad. Exams love pairing this with the wrong Upanishad — the answer stays Mundaka.

questions.question: The National Song 'Vande Mataram' originally appeared in which novel?
questions.rationale: Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay wrote it into his 1882 novel Anandamath, about sanyasis rebelling during the Bengal famine.

questions.question: Which of the following is India's national aquatic animal?
questions.rationale: The Ganges river dolphin (Platanista gangetica), declared the national aquatic animal in 2009, is nearly blind and navigates by echolocation.

questions.question: The full version of the National Anthem takes approximately how long to play?
questions.rationale: The full anthem runs roughly 52 seconds; a shortened ~20-second version exists for specific occasions. The two durations are a favourite exam pair.

questions.question: The Lion Capital of Sarnath, adopted as the State Emblem, belongs to the reign of which ruler?
questions.rationale: The polished-sandstone capital was carved around 250 BCE during Ashoka's reign, and the emblem version was adopted on 26 January 1950.

questions.question: India's national calendar, adopted in 1957, is based on which era?
questions.rationale: The Saka era counts from 78 CE; the national calendar's first month Chaitra begins on 22 March (21 March in a leap year).

questions.question: Which animal is India's National Heritage Animal?
questions.rationale: The Indian elephant was declared the National Heritage Animal in 2010 — a conservation-era addition the older books keep missing.
